recap:
Joe sits down with stand-up comic Brian Simpson on JRE 2266 to talk about comedy, the craft of stand-up, and Simpson's work in the Los Angeles comedy scene. Simpson, who hosts the improvised comedy show 'Bottom of the Barrel' at the Comedy Mothership and runs his own podcast 'BS with Brian Simpson,' brings genuine energy to the conversation about what it takes to make it as a comedian.

The episode digs into Simpson's approach to comedy and his new Netflix special 'Brian Simpson: Live from the Mothership,' which showcases his work in front of live audiences. They talk about the difference between comedy club performances and other venues, the importance of crowd work, and how comedians develop their material over time. Simpson shares stories about the comedy grind, bombing on stage, and learning from those experiences.

The conversation explores the improvisation aspects of Simpson's Bottom of the Barrel show, where comedians perform without a script and have to think on their feet. This leads into broader discussion about comedy as an art form, what audiences want, and how the comedy landscape has changed. They touch on the comedy community in LA, working with other comedians, and the kind of support system that exists among performers.

Throughout the episode, Simpson brings authenticity to the discussion, talking candidly about the ups and downs of comedy careers and what keeps comedians going despite the challenges. The conversation feels natural and conversational, with both Joe and Brian riffing on comedy topics and sharing perspectives on the craft that makes comedy work at different levels.
